title: Psychiatry
description: Psychiatry — mental health conditions, diagnosis and management.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old healthy man presents to the clinic with a 2-year history of worsening sad mood, poor appetite, insomnia, fatigue, low self-esteem, and feeling of hopelessness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her mother with a bald patch on her scalp. Her mother noted that she plucks her hair while studying and under stress. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 20-year-old man presents to the clinic with poor personal hygiene, echolalia, echopraxia, muttering to self, being in an odd posture for hours, and insomnia for the past 2 months. On examination, his orientation and memory are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the Primary Health Care Clinic with symptoms of anxiety due to difficulties in her relationship with her co-workers. Her examination was normal and the doctor has decided that there is no need for any investigation. Which of the following would be the most effective approach for consultation?

options.text: Instructing how to deal with others

questions.stem: A 55-year-old smoker presents to the Primary Health Care Clinic for the result of the biopsy of a lesion in his right lung. When informed that he had cancer in his right lung, he asked with anxiety, "Is it a mistake?" Which of the following is the most appropriate description for the patient's reaction?

A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 10-month history of restlessness, difficulty concentrating, and disturbance in his sleep pattern. He is diagnosed with generalised anxiety disorder. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

An 18-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with a 1-week history of euphoria, increased blood pressure, tachycardia, nausea, weight loss, psychomotor agitation, chills, sweating, and visual hallucinations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman is admitted to the Psychiatric Unit after causing superficial lacerations to her wrists. The reason is that she felt that her therapist has abandoned her. She has a depressed mood that varies by the hour. On admission, she claimed that she had heard a voice speaking. To her, although she currently denies it. She caused a disagreement between the psychiatric resident and the nursing staff, who have conflicting views of her behaviour in the unit. Which of the following personality disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with irritability, suspiciousness, activity and poor hygiene. Emergency Department doctors regarded his behaviour as abnormal and called for a psychiatrist. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of reduced energy, lack of enjoyment, reduced sleep, reduced appetite, suicidal ideas and lack of self-confidence. Examination and lab results are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old was brought to the Emergency Department complaining that his neighbors were trying to harm him and plotting to kill him. On questioning, he was very sure about this and said that he is still hearing their voices talking with each other, though none of them were present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman presents to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic with a history of psychomotor excitation and irritability. She has grandiose delusions and auditory hallucinations. On a mental state examination, she exhibited a lack of insight and flight of ideas. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 2-year history of getting orgasms too readily during the sexual act. He complains that during the sexual intercourse, he is having palpitations and worrying thoughts in his mind all the time. On examination, he has normal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl presents for a follow-up visit complaining that she is unable to eat because of an intense desire to reduce her weight. Sometimes, she develops an impulse to eat excessively, and she then follows the impulse. She then intermittently self-induces vomiting. On examination, she looked weak. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

15– A 20-year-old student presents to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic complaining that she feels embarrassed, dizzy, and tremulous whenever she tries to answer verbally in the classroom. Which of the following is the best treatment?

A 21-year-old man with depression presents for a follow-up visit. During the consultation, the psychiatrist asked, "Do you think that you are mentally ill?" Which of the following findings does the psychiatrist want to assess?

A 23-year-old college student was brought to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic with a 3-month history of persecutory delusions, hearing voices commenting on his actions, and disorganised behaviour without disturbance of mood, then returning to normal with no medication. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man presents to the clinic for a routine visit. During the consultation, he speaks loudly and rapidly without completely expressing one thought before beginning another. Speech patterns are rhyming, and the patient is easily distracted by cues in the immediate surroundings. Which of the following is the most likely description for these findings?

A 22-year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of approaching strangers and asking them the same inappropriate questions without stopping when instructed to do so. The patient seemed unaware of the fact that this was an inappropriate behaviour. Which of the following is the most likely description of this behaviour?
Which of the following conditions is most often associated with manic behaviour?

A 21-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of changes in the voice that she hears. Until now, it had been merely making critical comments about everything she did. For the past 2 weeks, however, she thinks the voices seemed to have been able to "suck thoughts out" of her and send them to others. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of unusual behaviour. He keeps a blanket over the television, believing that the government uses the actors to spy on the TV. He believes that the instructions to cover the TV came from God, who spoke through the light bulb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old healthy man complains of episodes of chest tightness, palpitations, dizziness and breathlessness. These episodes resolved after about 5 minutes. He remains normal between episodes, and the interval may extend for several days before a new episode occurs. He has Had constant anxiety about having another attack and felt sad about the situation. The patient cannot identify a triggering mechanism. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man has a history of pancreatic carcinoma and reports having lost all his prescriptions. He says that despite having recently completed chemotherapy, he has developed new symptoms and is afraid of a recurrence. There is no medical records for him in the hospitals. When confronted with this information, the patient ran away from the clinic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 2-month history of sleep disturbance, loss of interest, low energy, poor memory, and suicidal ideation. On examination, she looks weak and inactive. Laboratory investigations are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old healthy man is brought to the clinic for evaluation of progressive erratic behaviour. Over the past 4 months, he has believed that people on television are reading his thoughts. He expressed the presence of supernatural powers and that he has begun to act out in response to these ideations. He has not caused injuries, but the trends are becoming more violent. On examination, he is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan for major depression?

options.text: Select any drug to start, as all have equal efficacy
Initiate therapy with one medication for 2 weeks
Change medications if the patient doesn't respond

questions.stem: Which of the following systems is stimulated by stressful situations?

A 30-year-old man presents to the Outpatient Clinic with manifestations of opioid withdrawal. After full investigations, he was diagnosed as a heroin addict. As part of the rehabilitation process, he was prescribed a substitute for the addictive drug. Which of the following drugs should be prescribed?
Which of the following is described as "False belief not in accordance with a person's intelligence or culture"?

A 65-year-old man with congestive heart failure and osteoarthritis moved into a nursing home 3 months ago. During the past 4 weeks, the patient has lost 3.6 kg, lost interest in all social activities, and has been crying almost every day. The mood is worse in the morning. At times, especially when the mood is impaired, the patient's short-term memory appears to be lost. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old girl presents with a 12 kg weight loss over the last 6 months. She feels fat with an intense fear of gaining weight. Over the last 4 months, the patient has had amenorrhea. On examination, she has lanugo hair distribution. Height 16ti cm weight 42 kg Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic with recurrent attacks of palpitations, chest pain, difficulty in breathing, and a fear of dying. She also trembles and experiences numbness and tingling sensations in the hands and feet. The past medical history is not significant. On examination, she looks tense, and her hands are cold with fine tremors. Heart rate 108 /min, regular Temperature 3ti.2° C Blood pressure 120/82 mmHg Respiratory rate 14 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of intense fear before giving classes as a teacher in a secondary school. He claims that it is only a matter of time before a major teaching mistake is made. Which of the following phobias is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with 2 2-month history of anxiety, irritability, impotence, difficulty in sleeping, and a weight loss of 10 kg. There is no evidence of marital disharmony or any external causes for the patient's anxiety. The physical examination was normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely characteristic of a major depressive illness?

A 52-year-old woman presents with a 5-day history of insomnia and crying because of the death of a sibling. The patient has not slept for the last 2 days. Which of the following is the most appropriate short course of therapy?
Which of the following factors indicates a poor prognosis for schizophrenia?
A 27-year-old man who lost his spouse 2 months ago after a prolonged illness presents with a sad mood, decreased appetite, and sleep disturbance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following drug mechanisms of action is most appropriate to treat obsessional behavioural disorder?
Which of the following medications causes insomnia, anxiety and restlessness?

A 60-year-old man newly diagnosed with depression started on 30 mg amitriptyline each night. Shortly after the beginning of treatment, he complained of dizziness every morning. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Change to a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
Advise to take the medication with food
Advice to take the medication in the morning
Change amitriptyline dose to 10 mg 3 times a day

questions.stem: Which of the following is a potential side effect of amitriptyline?

A 12-year-old obese boy presents to the Primary Care Clinic with a history of being teased by children at school and, as a result, has considered "taking a lot of pills to just go to sleep and not wake up." Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the Primary Health Care Centre complaining of loss of interest and pleasure in daily activities for 3 weeks. She also complains that she has difficulty concentrating and sleeping. Further, she has also expressed that she feels that she is worthless in the world and, therefore, wants to end her life. Which of the following biochemical substance deficiency is the most likely cause?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the Primary Health Care Centre complaining of loss of interest and pleasure in daily activities for 3 weeks. She also complains that she has difficulty concentrating and sleeping. Further, she has also expressed that she feels that she is worthless in the world and, therefore, wants to end her life. Which of the following reuptake inhibitors is the best treatment?
Which of the following antipsychotic medications is most likely to cause weight gain?

A 35-year-old depressed housewife was started with antidepressants. After 2 weeks of taking the medication, the patient started complaining of constipation. Which of the following groups of antidepressants is the most likely cause?

A 15-year-old girl who had a serious disagreement with her friend. She did not want to meet her friend or talk to her anymore. If the girl saw her friend coming towards her or sing in a room, she would move away and not go in that direction. Which of the following defence mechanisms is the most likely explanation for this behaviour?

A 65-year-old man with depression presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit. The physician did his consultation using a bio-psycho-social model of treatment. Which of the following is a characteristic of this treatment model?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of extreme fear of going to the park, the zoo and sporting events. This has worsened to the point where she has stopped going out of the house. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents in an anxious, tearful state. He complains of chronic upper abdominal pain and is certain that he has stomach cancer, but no one believes him. He has seen 6 different physicians in the past year and has had a Gl series and barium enema performed, an ultrasound of the abdomen twice, and a CT scan. The patient was thinking of going to a herbal clinic next. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old woman delivered a full-term infant. On examination, he has an epicanthic fold, delayed milestones, a flat facial profile, simian palmar creases and an atrial septal defect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl is brought by her father to the Emergency Department with complaints of tachypnoea, light-headedness, paraesthesia and palpitations. Her father gives the history of her recent failure in her math test. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 1-month history of low mood and lack of sleep. It was associated with weight gain, isolation and concentration impairment. His wife mentioned that he bought a very expensive car and thought that he was a wealthy man 3 months ago. He is very talkative and difficult to interrupt. Which of the following medications is the most effective for long-term management?

A 23-year-old woman with frequent panic attacks presents to the clinic and complains that during her last attack 3 days ago, she felt that she was disconnected from the world as if the environment was strange. Which of the following would best describe her feelings?
A 30-year-old man has a personality disorder, which is characterised by being aggressive and violent. Which of the following is the most likely associated with violence?

A 10-year-old boy comes with his uncle for follow-up after a major car accident where he lost his mother and his 2 brothers. The uncle is worried after receiving a teacher's note regarding child behavior in the class. Teacher wrote that the child becomes unresponsive sometimes, has a lapse in attention. He stares at nothing, and act as if he just woke up in response to being called to attention. Which of the following terms describe a child's response mechanism?

A 2-month-old infant is brought to Well Baby Clinic by her mother because she is crying intensely recently and is not sleeping well overnight. The mother gave history of normal feeding. no fever or vomiting. These crying episodes are 2 to 3 times per week, last for 1 to 2 hours since the age of 1 month. Which of the following is the recommended revealing measure?
A 3-year-old girl is seen in the clinic. The mother gives history of yelling, hitting and saying "no" with other oppositional behaviours. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2.5-year-old girl seen in the screening clinic. The mother gave history of yelling, hitting and saying "no" with other oppositional behaviours. Which of the following is the most appropriate counselling should be given?

A 10-years-old boy diagnosed attention deficit hyperactivity disorders, presents with his mother the clinic. She complains about his behavior. She is advised to identify and reward positive behaviors and ignore disruptive. Which of the following helps to achieve this advice?
A 2-year-old boy presents with his mother complains that her child rebelling constantly with temper tantrums. What is the most appropriate counseling should be given?

options.text: Set limits on the child's behavior
Punish the child every time the child says "no*
Allow the behavior because this is normal at this age period

questions.stem: A 6-year old girl presents to the clinic with malnutrition. She seems to be neglected with poor hygiene. Her mother expresses feeling anxious and busy with other children at home with poor social circumstances. During consultation, it is essential to explore the mother's perspective, feeling. ideas and beliefs. Which of the following is the best next step?

options.text: Encourage the mother to use her own words to clarify the issues

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy brought by concerned mother for an evaluation her son's problem of 3 months after the death of his friend in a car accident, reluctantly mentioned to his mother that he wished he were dead, but would never do anything about these wishes. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Asking him about his suicide may increase the risk
Indirect inquiries about his suicide risk will foster rapport
Since this is a normal grief reaction, he should be left alone
Detailed questions about his suicidality are essential for prevention

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Department with chest pain, nausea, dizziness, and sweating. She states that she is afraid he is going to die. History includes 3 previous episodes during the past 2 months, each episode lasting about 15 minutes. She has been afraid to visit the doctor but she has become more afraid during the past month of having yet another episode. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 7-year-old boy with a diagnosis of separation anxiety. The mother asks for consultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate strategy that the mother should do?

options.text: Let your child focus on what unlikely bad things might happen
Let your child stay home when he does not want to go to school
Punish for behaviors that are a result of separation anxiety/fears
Help him think of ways a favorite superhero might handle the situation

questions.stem: Which of the following is the peak of nicotine withdrawal symptoms after smoking cessation?
Which of the following is an alternative treatment for severe depression?
Which of the following is the antidote for an opiate overdose?
Which of the following is the most likely side effect of bupropion when prescribed for smoking cessation?

A 24-year-old inactive woman presents to the clinic with 5-month history of amenorrhea. On examination, she has a body mass index of 20, stable for the last 5 years (see lab results). Pregnancy test: Negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man complains of having an unusually prominent jaw. He has been seen by 3 plastic surgeons, but each one has refused to do anything. On examination, he appears depressed and has no visible protrusion, the jaw and face are normal. He has past medical history of rhinoplasty and blepharoplasty. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old man presents to the clinic requesting a complete examination to exclude colon cancer. He recently had some investigations done and provided a list of test results. He complains that this fear is interfering severely with his work and social activities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old boy learns about the death of his father and within hours, his speech becomes disorganized, he is walking outside of his house with no clothes on, and he claims that his father is inside the house and telling him to do these things in his honour. The symptoms resolved after 3 days, and the son returned to full pre-morbid level of function but is obviously confused over the events of the past few days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a predilection of the feeling of hopelessness?

A 20-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, localized weakness to the right leg, and has a history of irregular menses. In the past, she has sought treatment for head, back, joint, and chest pain. Factitious disorder and malingering have been excluded as diagnoses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following investigations should be recommended for elderly patient with cognitive deficit?

An 8-year-old boy recently moved to another city. Soon after moving, school started, but the boy hesitated to make friends with anyone and had a hard time paying attention in class. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old man presents for a routine visit, while reporting his medical history, he reveals a significant alcohol intake. The physician wants to assess the drinking further using the cut- annoyed-guilty-eye (CAGE) screening questionnaire. Which of the following is a question in the CAGE screening questionnaire?

options.text: "Do you eat more after you drink?"
"Do you think you are an alcoholic?"
"Have you ever felt guilty about your drinking?"

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman presents to the clinic with 8-month history of irritability, excessive worry, and difficulty falling asleep and concentrating. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman is concerned about losing her job because of tiredness and would like to take antidepressants because of having a difficult time falling asleep and getting up in the morning. Her sleep disturbance is related to the inability to relax after getting into bed. She repeatedly checks to make sure that the door is locked, the oven is off, and the children's school supplies are organized. A similar routine occurs in the morning. She states that her behaviour is out of control but if is not done, she will not be able to sleep or leave the house. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old healthy man presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of feeling depressed. He is distressed at work and burnt-out. 4 months earlier, he was promoted to a managerial position and was having an interpersonal conflict with 2 of the employees. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

An 18-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 20-minute history of light- headedness, headaches, and nausea. He complains of tingling around the mouth and in the fingertips. On examination, he is anxious, tremulous, sweating, and breathing heavily. Which of the following is the most appropriate first action?

options.text: Patient rebreathe into a paper bag

questions.stem: Which of the following atypical antipsychotic agents is associated with the most weight gain?
Which of the following is the best treatment for a generalized anxiety disorder?
For which of the following childhood psychiatric disorders, clozapine is the most appropriate medication?
Which of the following antidepressants has a high efficacy in childhood and adolescent depression?
A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic with 3-month history of aliens taking to him and putting thoughts into his mind? Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of difficulty maintaining erections and impotence that occurs during stressful periods of life. He is currently under stress at work. On examination, he has normal physical findings. Which of the following is the first step in management?

options.text: Refer to a urologist for evaluation

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of recurrent intense fear accompanied by irritability, excessive worry, palpitations, and chest tightness. She is avoiding social gathering fearing of having same symptoms. Physical examination findings are normal. Which of the following medications is the most appropriate first line of treatment?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother with history of impaired language development, impaired intelligence, compulsive repetitive behaviour, and a preoccupation with inanimate objects. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A mother of a 3 month-old baby presents to the clinic and tells the physician that she is "going crazy." She states that since the baby has been born, she has continuously visualized a snake crawling into the baby's crib at night. She states that she knows it is not likely to happen but cannot get the thought out of her mind. She checks the baby's crib up to 50 times per night to ensure that there is no snake. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of anxiety. 2 months ago, during a meeting at her job, she became very anxious, sweaty, and short of breath. She had to leave the meeting in order to calm down. Since then, she has avoided meeting rooms out of fear that she will have a recurrence of her symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of gradual fear of automobiles. He has always been anxious of cars, but now can no longer look at them without experiencing shortness of breath, sweating, and fear. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of red dry skin on her hands. She washes her hands up to 70 times per day because she always feels dirty. Washing her hands relieves her anxiety, but as she touches anything, she wants to wash again. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man with a history of drug abuse presents to the clinic weekly with a variety of health complaints, which vary each time, and are greatly exaggerated. When he is unaware of being observed he appears asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman presents to the clinic for a routine physical check-up. On examination, she has fine hair all over the body. She feels fat and subsequently diets. BMI 16.8 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman calls the clinic expressing fear of leaving the house, and has been inside for 2 months. She becomes anxious at the thought of walking out the front door and is now unable to enter the room containing the front door. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of sweating, palpitations, nausea, and a "panicky feeling" when required to deliver a speech at work. He has no other difficulties at work. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of constant counting of floor tiles, cars, items on a dinner plate, and words in a conversation. She is upset by the counting but becomes anxious and agitated when she tries to stop herself from counting. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old came in active labor at 38 weeks of gestation. It was found that she is having an intrauterine fetal death. The bad news were delivered to her in steps. After delivery she insisted that the baby should be taken to Intensive Care Unit on a ventilator as she believes that he is not really dead. Which of the following best describes her condition?

A 12-year-old obese girl brought by her mother, 5-month after her menarche with irregular menstrual bleeding and increased weight. She has mild acne. The patient was uncomfortable, agitated and unable to cooperate to physical examination. BMI 26 kg/m2 What is the most likely disorder to be considered in communicating with this patient?

A 21-year-old woman married for 6 months brought to the Emergency Department by police with bruises on the face, chest and both hands. On examination, she looks sad with tears, sitting quite, and facing down to the floor. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach for history and examination?

options.text: Invest time with clinical findings at the beginning
Explore and identify her sadness and find out more what is causing it
Introducing yourself with a big smile and proceed to a chief complain
History and examination should be with the presence of the family member

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother. She noticed that the child has been eating clay and paper for the last 4 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of extreme fear of going to the park, the zoo and sporting events. This has worsened to the point where she has stopped going out of the house. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents in an anxious, tearful state. He complains of chronic, upper abdominal pain and is certain that he has stomach cancer but no one believes him. He has seen 6 different physicians in the past year and has had a Gl series and barium enema performed an ultrasound of the abdomen twice and a CT scan. The patient was thinking of next going to a Herbal Clinic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl is brought by her father to the Emergency Department with complaints of tachypnoea, light-headedness, paraesthesia and palpitations. Her father gives the history that she has recently failed her math test Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 1-month history of low mood and lack of sleep. It was associated with weight gain, isolation and concentration impairment. His wife mentioned that he bought a very expensive car and thinking that he is a wealthy man 3 months ago. He is very talkative and difficult to interrupt. Which of the following medications is the most effective for long-term management?
Which of the following is the diagnostic criteria for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children, according to the International Classification of Diseases-10?

A 23-year-old woman with frequent panic a]acks, presents to the clinic complaining that during her last attack 3 days ago she felt that she was disconnected from the world, as if the environment is strange. Which of the following would best describe her feelings?
Which of the following is associated with dyslexia?

options.text: Defect in visual or hearing acuity

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely clinical presentation of a delusional patient ?

A 7-year-old boy is brought by his mother because he was unable to sit in school without interrupting the class, wandering around the classroom or poking his neighbours. On examination, he has normal growth parameters. Which of the following is the best management?

A 30-year-old woman presents with a complaint of lower back pain for 1 year. During the last 2 years, she had presented with recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, headache and migratory joint pain. Her menstrual periods are irregular and heavy. She was terminated twice from the job due to frequent absence from the work. She is upset that proper diagnosis or treatment was not given to her. She had multiple laboratory tests done during the last 2 years and all were normal. The physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man with bronchial asthma presents with a 5-year history of severe anxiety in social gatherings. He often has sweating and palpitation when he leads discussions at work. He prefers to sit alone at home. He notices that his presenting complaint is provoked by salbutamol. His physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

A 28-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, treated for 6 months, presents for follow-up visit. On examination, she has 8 kg weight gain, generalized weakness and hair loss. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
A 56-year-old man with schizophrenia is started on neuroleptic medications to treat his psychotic symptoms. Which of the following side effects is the patient at greatest risk?
Which of the following is the most likely benefit of using antipsychotic therapy in schizophrenic patients?

A 23-year-old man is brought to the psychiatrist clinic because for the first time he started to hear some voices talking to him with unknown sources. On examination, he was apathetic and emotionally withdrawn. Which of the following is the best management?

A 45-year-old man with recurrent episodes of schizophrenia is on maintenance therapy to maintain suppression of symptoms, prevent relapse, improve quality of life, and support engagement in psychosocial therapy. Which of the following is the best outcome following the maintenance therapy?

options.text: 70% will have a satisfactory quality of life

questions.stem: Which of the following selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors is the most toxic in overdose?

A 23-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia based on the presence of both negative and positive symptoms of schizophrenia. Which of the following is the most effective medication?
Which of the following is the lowest fatal dose of tricyclic antidepressants?

An 8-year-old girl complaints of recurrent periumbilical pain lasting for 10-15 min morning time, no vomiting or loose stools. Abdomen examination is normal. Urine and stool analysis are normal. Mother says this pain is only during school days. Counseling to the mother and the teacher to manage school phobia/refusal includes behavior-management strategies such as providing positive reinforcements. Which of the following is an example of positive reinforcements?

options.text: Allow student to have more TV time at home
Comments focus on what the student did right
Give the student moderately challenging task to perform
Keep records of number of absent days during the semester

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy presents with his mother to outpatient clinic with malnutrition, he seems to be neglected with poor hygiene. Which of the following is an important skill needed to conduct consultation?

options.text: Lay out the consulting room with toys
Ask the mother to leave the room
Call the nurse to take vital signs, height and weight
Put aside time at the beginning to build rapport with him

questions.stem: A 42 hours-old full-term infant has not yet passed meconium was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis after Sweat chloride test. Family meetings with parents to discuss the diagnosis, management plan. The physician pulls together the main ideas, plan of management, prognosis and feelings of the parents to show understanding. Which of the following describe the technique in this communication skill?

A 14-month-old child is brought by his father with 2nd degree burns on both feet. He states that the child dipped in very hot bathtub water. There is a clear distinction line on the burn with no splash burns. There are other bruises on the child's limbs of different age. Child abuse suspected. Which of the following is the correct order of the four important advocacy skills for mandated reporters of child abuse?

options.text: Documenting, confirming, reporting. conferencing with parents
Observing. gathering information, making referrals, following up
Observing, making referrals, gathering information, following up

questions.stem: Surgical intern is assigned to stay with a 6-year-old boy who is waiting to have surgery to repair a cleft palate. The boy does not speak Arabic and appears anxious. The charge nurse has requested a translator but the translator has not yet arrived. Which of the following is the most appropriate action for the intern to do?

options.text: Insert IV cannula and start preanesthetic
Sedate the child to decrease her anxiety level
Suggest that the nurse stay with the child so that he can review her chart
Listen to the child's heart with a stethoscope and then let the child try to use the stethoscope to listen to his heart

questions.stem: An effective interviewing skill behaviors of listening carefully by entering the world of the patient and communicating that you imagine the patients world as the patient sees and experiences it. Yet, not becoming the patient and remain separate from the patient. Which of the following is the communication skill described above?

A 61-year-old man presents with history of constantly thinks about aliens landing in his backyard, especially when away from home. Despite knowing that aliens do not exist, he feels overwhelmed with the idea that they have landed. He fears that he is "going insane" Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of hearing voices coming from the toaster and refrigerator, warning that all the food is poisoned. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic for routine check-up. On examination, he kept looking to the right frequently. When questioned, he said, "My mother is there, but no one can see her except me". He claims that she comes and goes, even though the family indicates she died when the patient was a child. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old man presents to the clinic for a routine physical check-up. He has a history of pulling out hair when under stress. On examination, he has diffuse hair thinning along with the absence of eyelashes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old girl presents to the clinic with history of tetany, swollen glands, and eroded dental enamel (see lab result). Electrolytes test Result Normal Value Potassium 2.8 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
